newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares, lira off after JCR downgrades debt.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares, lira off after JCR downgrades debt.

text.p: Turkish shares dived by more than three percent and the lira weakened against the dollar after Japan's JCR agency downgraded Turkey's debt rating to BB from BB+, bankers and brokers said on Tuesday.
"The JCR news sparked panic sales and turned the market sentiment to pessimistic from optimistic," said Bulent Onder from Acar securities.
The composite index at Istanbul's stock exchange dropped 3.48 percent from Monday before rebounding slightly to end morning trading at 80,698.52, down 2,474.27 points or 2.97 percent.
The lira eased to 99,400 against the dollar from 99,300 at the opening and 99,260 at Monday's close after the JCR announcement, prompting immediate central bank intervention.
It firmed to 99,330 after the central bank began selling dollars for lira to banks.
"The dollar moved upwards on JCR news, but the central bank stepped in to control its rise. Treasury-bill rates also fluctuated briefly," said one banker.
T-bill and bond yields which opened lower on buying, firmed slightly after the JCR statement, but later settled at lower levels when compared to Monday.
